extracted.intended_audience: readers and correspondents of The Spectator; literate early-18th-century public interested in manners, taste, and periodical essays
extracted.subtask_description: An early-18th-century Spectator essay laying out the paper's editorial stance (what it will and will not publish) and offering prescriptive commentary on manners, dress, clubs, and musical/theatrical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on passions not fashions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not my intention to sink the Dignity of this my Paper with Reflections upon Red-heels or Top-knots, but rather to enter into the Passions of Mankind, and to correct those depraved Sentiments that give Birth to all those little Extravagancies which appear in their outward Dress and Behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay will address the underlying motives and sentiments (vanity, pride) that produce fashionable excesses rather than merely satirising individual trimmings. Examples and analogy: a physician treats constitution, a surgeon treats outward blotches; the author prefers to 'sweeten the Blood and rectify the Constitution' rather than only prune trimmings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy root causes of affected dress
rubrics_metrics.description: Foppish and fantastick Ornaments are only Indications of Vice, not criminal in themselves. Extinguish Vanity in the Mind, and you naturally retrench the little Superfluities of Garniture and Equipage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and correct vanity and the social dispositions that produce extravagant dress rather than punishing or obsessing over the dress itself. The observable anti-pattern is targeting accessories (red-heels, fringed gloves) without addressing the inner disposition that creates demand for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Censor of small Wares (institutional remedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have Thoughts of creating an Officer under me to be entituled, 'The Censor of small Wares', and of allotting him one Day in a Week for the Execution of such his Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical proposal for policing or publicly satirising fashionable excesses on a regular basis; the officer would operate like a surgeon treating outward blemishes while the author works on deeper causes. The suggestion is presented as tentative and subject to readers' approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial prohibition on private scandal and defamation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not my Design to be a Publisher of Intreagues and Cuckoldoms, or to bring little infamous Stories out of their present lurking Holes into broad Day light. If I attack the Vicious, I shall only set upon them in a Body: and will not be provoked by the worst Usage that I can receive from others, to make an Example of any particular Criminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper will refuse to print private lampoons, slanders, and intimate calumnies about named individuals or families; when vice is attacked it will be treated as a species or social problem rather than singling out individuals. Prevents publisher from succumbing to the circulation/traffic advantages of private defamation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid party-political partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: As I am very sensible my Paper would lose its whole Effect, should it run into the Outrages of a Party, I shall take Care to keep clear of every thing which looks that Way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorially remain an unconcerned spectator on party divisions: do not inflame feuds or take partisan sides. The aim is to assuage private inflammations and allay public ferments rather than exacerbate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite harmless contributions and assist their development
rubrics_metrics.description: If he has started any Hint which he is not able to pursue... if he has discovered any epidemical Vice which has escaped my Observation, or has heard of any uncommon Virtue which he would desire to publish... if he has any Materials that can furnish out an innocent Diversion, I shall promise him my best Assistance in the working of them up for a publick Entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper solicits correspondents' harmless anecdotes, hints, or reports of social vices/virtues and offers editorial help to shape them into publishable pieces. This clarifies submission scope (innocent diversion rather than private scandal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ugly Club admission rules (Act of Deformity)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. That no Person whatsoever shall be admitted without a visible Quearity in his Aspect... II. That a singular Regard be had... to the Gibbosity of the Gentlemen... or to the Obliquity of their Figure... III. That if the Quantity of any Man's Nose be eminently miscalculated... _Lastly_, That if there shall be two or more Competitors for the same Vacancy, caeteris paribus, he that has the thickest Skin to have the Preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific membership criteria for the University 'Ugly Club': visible oddity of aspect judged by officers (president casting vote); emphasis on hump/obliquity or ill-shaped nose; where tied, preference to the toughest-skinned (able to bear ridicule). Rituals: new members must provide a dish of codfish and a speech in praise of Æsop; plans to decorate the club-room with famous ill-favoured heads; encouragement (mock) of female applicants under a statute. The Act blends evaluation criteria with ceremonial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-deprecation as the best expedient for deformity
rubrics_metrics.description: When he can possess himself with such a Chearfulness, Women and Children, who were at first frighted at him, will afterwards be as much pleased with him... The best Expedient therefore is to be pleasant upon himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social conduct guideline: those with natural defects should adopt a light, self-deprecating humour rather than being abashed or overly sensibl e about features they cannot change. Examples cited: Scarron, Prince Harry and Falstaff, and anecdotes of men turning ridicule into wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opera translation and production principles (preserve sense and intelligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: That nothing is capable of being well set to Musick, that is not Nonsense. [satirical maxim quoted] Translators often made Words of their own... their chief Care being to make the Numbers of the English Verse answer to those of the Italian... the necessary Transposition of Words ... made the Musick appear very absurd in one Tongue that was very natural in the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding criticisms for opera practice: avoid prioritising metrical rhyme over sense when setting text to music (example: translation of 'Camilla' produced awkward mismatches where musical emphasis fell on wrong semantic words); avoid mixing languages on stage (Italian singers intermingled with English speakers produced incomprehensible dialogue). The essay recommends considering music and dramatic sense together and hints at forthcoming more detailed opinions on music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn against Music crowding out higher arts
rubrics_metrics.description: If it would take the entire Possession of our Ears... if it would exclude Arts that have a much greater Tendency to the Refinement of humane Nature: I must confess I would allow it no better Quarter than 'Plato' has done, who banishes it out of his Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative admonition: assess cultural tastes so that music does not monopolise public attention to the detriment of drama and other arts that refine the mind. The anti-pattern is elevating foreign musical fashions above native literary and dramatic excellence.
